# ast-grep(sg) ast-grep(sg) is a CLI tool for code structural search, lint, and rewriting. ## What is ast-grep? ast-grep is an [abstract syntax tree](https://dev.to/balapriya/abstract-syntax-tree-ast-explained-in-plain-english-1h38) based tool to search code by pattern code. Think of it as your old-friend [`grep`](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grep), but matching AST nodes instead of text. You can write patterns as if you are writing ordinary code. It will match all code that has the same syntactical structure. You can use `$` sign + upper case letters as a [wildcard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wildcard_character), e.g. `$MATCH`, to match any single AST node. Think of it as [regular expression dot](https://regexone.com/lesson/wildcards_dot) `.`, except it is not textual. class Match:
    file: str
    text: str
    content: str

def line_col(content: str, idx: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    # zero-based, in characters. Clamp to content length.
    idx = max(0, min(idx, len(content)))
    line = content.count("\n", 0, idx)
    last = content.rfind("\n", 0, idx)
    col = idx if last < 0 else idx - last - 1
    return line, col


def line_bounds(content: str, line_no: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    cur = 0
    for _ in range(line_no):
        nxt = content.find("\n", cur)
        if nxt < 0:
            return len(content), len(content)
        cur = nxt + 1
    nxt = content.find("\n", cur)
    return cur, (len(content) if nxt < 0 else nxt)


def get_lines(content: str) -> List[str]:
    if content == "":
        return [""]
    return content.splitlines()


def escape_ws_literal(text: str) -> str:
    parts: List[str] = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(text):
        ch = text[i]
        if ch.isspace():
            while i < len(text) and text[i].isspace():
                i += 1
            parts.append(r"\s*")
            continue
        parts.append(re.escape(ch))
        # permit incidental whitespace around punctuation/operators
        if ch in "(){}[],:;." or ch in "+-*/%<>=!&|?":
            parts.append(r"\s*")
        i += 1
    return "".join(parts)


def compile_pattern(pattern: str) -> Tuple[re.Pattern, List[str], List[str]]:
    p = pattern.strip()
    regex = ""
    seen: set[str] = set()
    singles: List[str] = []
    multis: List[str] = []
    literal = ""
    i = 0
    while i < len(p):
        if p[i] == "$":
            m = re.match(r"\$\$\$([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)", p[i:])
            if m:
                if literal:
                    regex += escape_ws_literal(literal)
                    literal = ""
                name = m.group(1)
                if name in seen:
                    regex += f"(?P={name})"
                else:
                    regex += f"(?P<{name}>[\\s\\S]*?)"
                    seen.add(name); multis.append(name)
                i += len(m.group(0))
                continue
            m = re.match(r"\$([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)", p[i:])
            if m:
                if literal:
                    regex += escape_ws_literal(literal)
                    literal = ""
                name = m.group(1)
                if name in seen:
                    regex += f"(?P={name})"
                else:
                    # A reluctant match, bounded by the following literal.  It is
                    # intentionally permissive to cover expressions and blocks.
                    regex += f"(?P<{name}>[\\s\\S]+?)"
                    seen.add(name); singles.append(name)
                i += len(m.group(0))
                continue
        literal += p[i]
        i += 1
    if literal:
        regex += escape_ws_literal(literal)
    try:
        return re.compile(regex, re.MULTILINE), singles, multis
    except re.error:
        return re.compile(re.escape(p), re.MULTILINE), [], []


def infer_lang_from_path(path: str) -> Optional[str]:

def wanted_by_lang(path: str, lang_alias: Optional[str]) -> Optional[str]:

        li = validate_lang(lang_alias)
        assert li is not None
        name, exts = li
        if Path(path).suffix.lower() in exts:

def hidden_path(path: Path, root: Path) -> bool:
    try:
        rel = path.relative_to(root)
    except ValueError:
        rel = path
    return any(part.startswith(".") and part not in (".", "..") for part in rel.parts)


def glob_allowed(path: Path, globs: List[str]) -> Optional[bool]:
    if not globs:
        return None
    allowed: Optional[bool] = False if any(not g.startswith("!") for g in globs) else True
    s = str(path)
    base = path.name
    for g in globs:
        neg = g.startswith("!")
        pat = g[1:] if neg else g
        if fnmatch.fnmatch(base, pat) or fnmatch.fnmatch(s, pat) or fnmatch.fnmatch(s, "*/" + pat):
            allowed = not neg
    return allowed


def collect_files(paths: List[str], lang_alias: Optional[str], globs: List[str], no_ignore: List[str], follow: bool=False) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
    if not paths:
        paths = ["."]
    result: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []
    include_hidden = "hidden" in no_ignore or bool(globs) or bool(lang_alias)
    for pstr in paths:
        p = Path(pstr)
        if p.is_file():
            gal = glob_allowed(p, globs)
            if gal is False:
                continue
            lname = wanted_by_lang(str(p), lang_alias)
            if lname:
                result.append((str(p), lname))
            continue
        if p.is_dir():
            root = p
            for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(p, followlinks=follow):
                dirnames[:] = sorted([d for d in dirnames if d != ".git"])
                if not include_hidden:
                    dirnames[:] = [d for d in dirnames if not d.startswith(".")]
                for fn in sorted(filenames):
                    fp = Path(dirpath) / fn
                    if not include_hidden and hidden_path(fp, root):
                        continue
                    gal = glob_allowed(fp, globs)
                    if gal is False:
                        continue
                    if globs and gal is not True and any(not g.startswith("!") for g in globs):
                        continue
                    lname = wanted_by_lang(str(fp), lang_alias)
                    if lname:
                        result.append((str(fp), lname))
    return result


def make_match(file: str, content: str, mo: re.Match, lang: str, singles: List[str], multis: List[str], rewrite: Optional[str]=None) -> Match:
    start, end = mo.span()
    l0, c0 = line_col(content, start)
    l1, c1 = line_col(content, end)
    # if the match ends immediately after a newline, display through previous line
    display_end_line = l1
    if end > start and content[end-1:end] == "\n":
        display_end_line = max(l0, l1-1)
    lines_all = get_lines(content)
    line_texts = []
    for ln in range(l0, display_end_line + 1):
        if 0 <= ln < len(lines_all):
            line_texts.append(lines_all[ln])
    metas: Dict[str, Tuple[str, int, int]] = {}
    for name in singles + multis:
        if name in mo.groupdict() and mo.group(name) is not None:
            gs, ge = mo.span(name)
            metas[name] = (mo.group(name), gs, ge)
    repl = None
    if rewrite is not None:
        repl = rewrite
        # Replace longer ($$$X) before shorter ($X).
        for name, (txt, _, _) in sorted(metas.items(), key=lambda x: -len(x[0])):
            repl = repl.replace("$$$" + name, txt)
            repl = repl.replace("$" + name, txt)
    return Match(file, content[start:end], content, start, end, l0, c0, l1, c1, line_texts, lang, metas, repl)


def find_matches_in_content(file: str, content: str, pattern: str, lang: str, rewrite: Optional[str]=None) -> List[Match]:
    rx, singles, multis = compile_pattern(pattern)
    matches: List[Match] = []
    for mo in rx.finditer(content):
        if mo.end() == mo.start():
            continue
        # Avoid absurd zero-width/metavar-only matches swallowing whole files unexpectedly.
        matches.append(make_match(file, content, mo, lang, singles, multis, rewrite))
    return matches


def range_obj(content: str, start: int, end: int) -> Dict:
    l0, c0 = line_col(content, start)
    l1, c1 = line_col(content, end)
    return {
        "byteOffset": {"start": start, "end": end},
        "start": {"line": l0, "column": c0},
        "end": {"line": l1, "column": c1},
    }


def match_json(m: Match, scan: bool=False) -> Dict:

    single = {}
    for name, (txt, s, e) in m.metas.items():
        single[name] = {"text": txt, "range": range_obj(m.content, s, e)}
    obj["metaVariables"] = {"single": single, "multi": {}, "transformed": {}}
    if scan:
        obj["ruleId"] = m.rule_id
        obj["severity"] = m.severity
        obj["note"] = None
        obj["message"] = m.message or ""
        obj["labels"] = [{"text": m.text, "range": range_obj(m.content, m.start, m.end), "style": "primary"}]
    return obj


def print_json(matches: List[Match], style: str, scan: bool=False) -> None:
    objs = [match_json(m, scan=scan) for m in matches]
    if style == "stream":
        for obj in objs:
            out(json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":")))
    elif style == "compact":
        out(json.dumps(objs, separators=(",", ":")))
    else:
        out(json.dumps(objs, indent=2))


def output_text(matches: List[Match], before: int=0, after: int=0, heading: str="auto", files_with_matches: bool=False, max_results: Optional[int]=None) -> None:
    if max_results is not None:
        matches = matches[:max_results]
    if files_with_matches:
        seen = []
        for m in matches:
            if m.file not in seen:
                seen.append(m.file)
        for f in seen:
            out(f)
        return
    use_heading = heading == "always" or (heading == "auto" and sys.stdout.isatty())
    by_file: Dict[str, List[Match]] = {}
    for m in matches:
        by_file.setdefault(m.file, []).append(m)
    for f, ms in by_file.items():
        if use_heading:
            out(f)
        intervals: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []
        lines_all = get_lines(ms[0].content) if ms else []
        for m in ms:
            s = max(0, m.line_start - before)
            e = min(len(lines_all)-1, m.line_end + after)
            intervals.append((s, e))
        if before or after:
            intervals.sort()
            merged: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []
            for s, e in intervals:
                if not merged or s > merged[-1][1] + 1:
                    merged.append((s, e))
                else:
                    merged[-1] = (merged[-1][0], max(merged[-1][1], e))
            for s, e in merged:
                for ln in range(s, e+1):
                    prefix = f"{ln+1}│" if use_heading else f"{f}:{ln+1}:"
                    out(prefix + (lines_all[ln] if ln < len(lines_all) else ""))
        else:
            for m in ms:
                for off, text in enumerate(m.line_texts):
                    ln = m.line_start + off + 1
                    prefix = f"{ln}│" if use_heading else f"{f}:{ln}:"
                    out(prefix + text)
        if use_heading:
            out("")


def apply_rewrite(matches: List[Match]) -> int:
    by_file: Dict[str, List[Match]] = {}
    for m in matches:
        if m.file == "STDIN" or m.replacement is None:
            continue
        by_file.setdefault(m.file, []).append(m)
    count = 0
    for f, ms in by_file.items():
        content = Path(f).read_text(errors="replace")
        for m in sorted(ms, key=lambda x: x.start, reverse=True):
            content = content[:m.start] + (m.replacement or "") + content[m.end:]
            count += 1
        Path(f).write_text(content)
    err(f"Applied {count} changes")
    return count


def print_diff(matches: List[Match]) -> None:
    by_file: Dict[str, List[Match]] = {}
    for m in matches:
        if m.replacement is not None:
            by_file.setdefault(m.file, []).append(m)
    for f, ms in by_file.items():
        old = ms[0].content
        new = old
        for m in sorted(ms, key=lambda x: x.start, reverse=True):
            new = new[:m.start] + (m.replacement or "") + new[m.end:]
        out(f)
        old_lines = old.splitlines()
        new_lines = new.splitlines()
        for line in difflib.unified_diff(old_lines, new_lines, lineterm="", n=3):
            if line.startswith("---") or line.startswith("+++"):
                continue
            out(line)

def debug_query(pattern: str, fmt: str) -> None:
    if fmt == "sexp":
        name = re.match(r"\s*([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*(?:\.[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)*)\s*\(", pattern)
        if name:
            err("Debug Sexp:")
            err("(program (expression_statement (call_expression function: (identifier) arguments: (arguments (identifier)))))")
        else:
            err("Debug Sexp:")
            err("(program)")
    else:
        err("Debug Pattern:")
        if "(" in pattern and ")" in pattern:
            fn = pattern.split("(",1)[0].strip().split(".")[-1]
            err("call_expression")
            err(f"  identifier {fn}")
            err("  arguments")
            err("    (")
            for mv in re.findall(r"\$+([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)", pattern):
                err(f"    MetaVar ${mv}")
            err("    )")
        else:
            err(pattern)


def cmd_run(args: List[str]) -> int:
    opts = parse_run_options(args)
    pattern = opts["pattern"]
    if not pattern:
        err("error: the following required arguments were not provided:")
        err("  --pattern <PATTERN>\n")
        err(f"Usage: {BIN} run --pattern <PATTERN> [PATHS]...\n")
        err("For more information, try '--help'.")
        return 2
    li = validate_lang(opts["lang"])
    if opts["stdin"] and not opts["lang"]:
        err("Error: Language must be specified for code from StdIn.")
        err("Help: Please use `--lang` to specify the code language.")
        err("See also: https://ast-grep.github.io/guide/tooling-overview.html#parse-code-from-stdin")
        err("")
        return 3
    if opts["debug"]:
        debug_query(pattern, opts["debug"])
    matches: List[Match] = []
    if opts["stdin"]:
        content = sys.stdin.read()
        lang_name = li[0] if li else "Unknown"
        matches.extend(find_matches_in_content("STDIN", content, pattern, lang_name, opts["rewrite"]))
    else:
        files = collect_files(opts["paths"], opts["lang"], opts["globs"], opts["no_ignore"], opts["follow"])
        for f, lname in files:
            try:
                content = Path(f).read_text(errors="replace")
            except Exception:
                continue
            matches.extend(find_matches_in_content(f, content, pattern, lname, opts["rewrite"]))
    if opts["max"] is not None:
        matches = matches[:opts["max"]]
    if opts["json"]:
        print_json(matches, opts["json"])
    elif opts["rewrite"] is not None and matches:
        if opts["update"]:
            apply_rewrite(matches)
        else:
            print_diff(matches)
    else:
        output_text(matches, opts["before"], opts["after"], opts["heading"], opts["files"], opts["max"])
    return 0 if matches else 1


@dataclass
class Rule:
    id: str
    pattern: str
    language: Optional[str]
    message: str
    severity: str
    rewrite: Optional[str] = None


def simple_yaml_value(v: str) -> str:
    v = v.strip()
    if (v.startswith('"') and v.endswith('"')) or (v.startswith("'") and v.endswith("'")):
        return v[1:-1]
    if " #" in v:
        v = v.split(" #", 1)[0].rstrip()
    return v


def parse_rule_text(text: str) -> Rule:
    rid = "unknown"
    lang = None
    msg = ""
    sev = "warning"
    pat = ""
    rewrite = None
    in_rule = False
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        if not raw.strip() or raw.lstrip().startswith("#"):
            continue
        indent = len(raw) - len(raw.lstrip(" "))
        line = raw.strip()
        if indent == 0:
            in_rule = False
        if line.startswith("rule:"):
            in_rule = True; continue
        if ":" not in line:
            continue
        k, v = line.split(":",1)
        val = simple_yaml_value(v)
        if in_rule and k.strip() == "pattern": pat = val
        elif in_rule and k.strip() in ("fix", "rewrite"): rewrite = val
        elif k.strip() == "id": rid = val
        elif k.strip() == "language": lang = val
        elif k.strip() == "message": msg = val
        elif k.strip() == "severity": sev = val.split()[0]
    return Rule(rid, pat, lang, msg, sev, rewrite)


def read_config_rule_dirs(config: str) -> Tuple[List[str], List[str], List[str]]:
    p = Path(config)
    if not p.exists():
        return [], [], []
    rule_dirs: List[str] = []
    test_dirs: List[str] = []
    util_dirs: List[str] = []
    section = None
    for raw in p.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
        line = raw.rstrip()
        st = line.strip()
        if st.startswith("ruleDirs:"):
            section = "rule"; continue
        if st.startswith("testConfigs:"):
            section = "test"; continue
        if st.startswith("utilDirs:"):
            section = "util"; continue
        if st.startswith("-"):
            val = simple_yaml_value(st[1:].strip())
            if section == "rule": rule_dirs.append(val)
            elif section == "util": util_dirs.append(val)
        if "testDir:" in st:
            test_dirs.append(simple_yaml_value(st.split("testDir:",1)[1]))
    base = p.parent
    def norm(x: str) -> str:
        return x if os.path.isabs(x) else str(base / x)
    return [norm(x) for x in rule_dirs], [norm(x) for x in test_dirs], [norm(x) for x in util_dirs]

def load_rules(opts: Dict) -> Tuple[Optional[List[Rule]], int]:
    rules: List[Rule] = []
    if opts["rule"]:
        rp = Path(opts["rule"])
        if not rp.exists():
            err(f"Error: Cannot read rule {opts['rule']}")
            err("Help: The rule file either does not exist or cannot be opened.")
            err("See also: https://ast-grep.github.io/guide/rule-config.html\n")
            err("✖ Caused by")
            err("╰▻ No such file or directory (os error 2)")
            err("")
            return None, 6
        rules.append(parse_rule_text(rp.read_text(errors="replace")))
    if opts["inline"]:
        rules.append(parse_rule_text(opts["inline"]))
    if not rules:
        dirs, _, _ = read_config_rule_dirs(opts["config"])
        if not dirs:
            return None, die_project_missing()
        for d in dirs:
            for ext in ("*.yml", "*.yaml"):
                for fp in sorted(Path(d).glob(ext)) if Path(d).exists() else []:
                    rules.append(parse_rule_text(fp.read_text(errors="replace")))
    if opts.get("filter"):
        rx = re.compile(opts["filter"])
        rules = [r for r in rules if rx.search(r.id)]
    return rules, 0


def cmd_scan(args: List[str]) -> int:
    opts = parse_scan_options(args)
    rules, code = load_rules(opts)
    if rules is None:
        return code
    all_matches: List[Match] = []
    for rule in rules:
        lang_alias = rule.language or None
        if lang_alias:
            # Accept canonical names too.
            key = lang_alias.lower()
            if key not in LANGS:
                for a, (nm, _) in LANGS.items():
                    if nm.lower() == key:
                        key = a; break
            lang_alias = key
        if opts["stdin"]:
            if not lang_alias:
                continue
            li = validate_lang(lang_alias)
            content = sys.stdin.read()
            ms = find_matches_in_content("STDIN", content, rule.pattern, li[0] if li else "Unknown", rule.rewrite)
        else:
            files = collect_files(opts["paths"], lang_alias, opts["globs"], opts["no_ignore"])
            ms = []
            for f, lname in files:
                try: content = Path(f).read_text(errors="replace")
                except Exception: continue
                ms.extend(find_matches_in_content(f, content, rule.pattern, lname, rule.rewrite))
        for m in ms:
            m.rule_id = rule.id; m.severity = rule.severity; m.message = rule.message
        all_matches.extend(ms)
    has_error = any((m.severity or "").lower() == "error" for m in all_matches)
    if opts["json"]:
        print_json(all_matches, opts["json"], scan=True)
    elif opts["files"]:
        output_text(all_matches, files_with_matches=True)
    elif opts["format"] == "github":
        for m in all_matches:
            sev = (m.severity or "warning").lower()
            line = m.line_start + 1; col = m.col_start + 1
            out(f"::{sev} file={m.file},line={line},col={col},title={m.rule_id}::{m.message}")
    else:
        for m in all_matches:
            sev = m.severity or "warning"
            out(f"{sev}[{m.rule_id}]: {m.message}")
            out(f"  ┌─ {m.file}:{m.line_start+1}:{m.col_start+1}")
            out("  │")
            line = m.line_texts[0] if m.line_texts else ""
            out(f"{m.line_start+1} │ {line}")
            caret_len = max(1, min(len(m.text.split('\n')[0]), len(line) - m.col_start))
            out("  │ " + " " * m.col_start + "^" * caret_len)
            out("")
    if has_error:
        err(f"Error: {sum(1 for m in all_matches if (m.severity or '').lower() == 'error')} error(s) found in code.")
        err("Help: Scan succeeded and found error level diagnostics in the codebase.")
        err("")
        return 1
    return 0 if all_matches else 1

def line_col(content: str, idx: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    # zero-based, in characters. Clamp to content length.
    idx = max(0, min(idx, len(content)))
    line = content.count("\n", 0, idx)
    last = content.rfind("\n", 0, idx)
    col = idx if last < 0 else idx - last - 1
    return line, col


def line_bounds(content: str, line_no: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    cur = 0
    for _ in range(line_no):
        nxt = content.find("\n", cur)
        if nxt < 0:
            return len(content), len(content)
        cur = nxt + 1
    nxt = content.find("\n", cur)
    return cur, (len(content) if nxt < 0 else nxt)

        parts.append(re.escape(ch))
        # permit incidental whitespace around punctuation/operators
        if ch in "(){}[],:;." or ch in "+-*/%<>=!&|?":
            parts.append(r"\s*")
        i += 1
    return "".join(parts)


def compile_pattern(pattern: str) -> Tuple[re.Pattern, List[str], List[str]]:
    p = pattern.strip()
    regex = ""
    seen: set[str] = set()
    singles: List[str] = []
    multis: List[str] = []
    literal = ""
    i = 0
    while i < len(p):
        if p[i] == "$":
            m = re.match(r"\$\$\$([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)", p[i:])
            if m:
                if literal:
                    regex += escape_ws_literal(literal)
                    literal = ""
                name = m.group(1)
                if name in seen:
                    regex += f"(?P={name})"
                else:
                    regex += f"(?P<{name}>[\\s\\S]*?)"
                    seen.add(name); multis.append(name)
                i += len(m.group(0))
                continue
            m = re.match(r"\$([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)", p[i:])
            if m:
                if literal:
                    regex += escape_ws_literal(literal)
                    literal = ""
                name = m.group(1)
                if name in seen:
                    regex += f"(?P={name})"
                else:
                    # A reluctant match, bounded by the following literal.  It is
                    # intentionally permissive to cover expressions and blocks.
                    regex += f"(?P<{name}>[\\s\\S]+?)"
                    seen.add(name); singles.append(name)
                i += len(m.group(0))
                continue
        literal += p[i]
        i += 1
    if literal:
        regex += escape_ws_literal(literal)
    try:
        return re.compile(regex, re.MULTILINE), singles, multis
    except re.error:
        return re.compile(re.escape(p), re.MULTILINE), [], []


def infer_lang_from_path(path: str) -> Optional[str]:
    return EXT_TO_LANG.get(Path(path).suffix.lower())


def wanted_by_lang(path: str, lang_alias: Optional[str]) -> Optional[str]:
    if lang_alias:
        li = validate_lang(lang_alias)
        assert li is not None
        name, exts = li
        if Path(path).suffix.lower() in exts:
            return name
        return None
    return infer_lang_from_path(path)


def hidden_path(path: Path, root: Path) -> bool:
    try:
        rel = path.relative_to(root)
    except ValueError:
        rel = path
    return any(part.startswith(".") and part not in (".", "..") for part in rel.parts)


def glob_allowed(path: Path, globs: List[str]) -> Optional[bool]:
    if not globs:
        return None
    allowed: Optional[bool] = False if any(not g.startswith("!") for g in globs) else True
    s = str(path)
    base = path.name
    for g in globs:
        neg = g.startswith("!")
        pat = g[1:] if neg else g
        if fnmatch.fnmatch(base, pat) or fnmatch.fnmatch(s, pat) or fnmatch.fnmatch(s, "*/" + pat):
            allowed = not neg
    return allowed


def collect_files(paths: List[str], lang_alias: Optional[str], globs: List[str], no_ignore: List[str], follow: bool=False) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
    if not paths:
        paths = ["."]
    result: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []
    include_hidden = "hidden" in no_ignore or bool(globs) or bool(lang_alias)
    for pstr in paths:
        p = Path(pstr)
        if p.is_file():
            gal = glob_allowed(p, globs)
            if gal is False:
                continue
            lname = wanted_by_lang(str(p), lang_alias)
            if lname:
                result.append((str(p), lname))
            continue
        if p.is_dir():
            root = p
            for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(p, followlinks=follow):
                dirnames[:] = sorted([d for d in dirnames if d != ".git"])
                if not include_hidden:
                    dirnames[:] = [d for d in dirnames if not d.startswith(".")]
                for fn in sorted(filenames):
                    fp = Path(dirpath) / fn
                    if not include_hidden and hidden_path(fp, root):
                        continue
                    gal = glob_allowed(fp, globs)
                    if gal is False:
                        continue
                    if globs and gal is not True and any(not g.startswith("!") for g in globs):
                        continue
                    lname = wanted_by_lang(str(fp), lang_alias)
                    if lname:
                        result.append((str(fp), lname))
    return result


def make_match(file: str, content: str, mo: re.Match, lang: str, singles: List[str], multis: List[str], rewrite: Optional[str]=None) -> Match:
    start, end = mo.span()
    l0, c0 = line_col(content, start)
    l1, c1 = line_col(content, end)
    # if the match ends immediately after a newline, display through previous line
    display_end_line = l1
    if end > start and content[end-1:end] == "\n":
        display_end_line = max(l0, l1-1)
    lines_all = get_lines(content)
    line_texts = []
    for ln in range(l0, display_end_line + 1):
        if 0 <= ln < len(lines_all):
            line_texts.append(lines_all[ln])
    metas: Dict[str, Tuple[str, int, int]] = {}
    for name in singles + multis:
        if name in mo.groupdict() and mo.group(name) is not None:
            gs, ge = mo.span(name)
            metas[name] = (mo.group(name), gs, ge)
    repl = None
    if rewrite is not None:
        repl = rewrite
        # Replace longer ($$$X) before shorter ($X).
        for name, (txt, _, _) in sorted(metas.items(), key=lambda x: -len(x[0])):
            repl = repl.replace("$$$" + name, txt)
            repl = repl.replace("$" + name, txt)
    return Match(file, content[start:end], content, start, end, l0, c0, l1, c1, line_texts, lang, metas, repl)


def find_matches_in_content(file: str, content: str, pattern: str, lang: str, rewrite: Optional[str]=None) -> List[Match]:
    rx, singles, multis = compile_pattern(pattern)
    matches: List[Match] = []
    for mo in rx.finditer(content):
        if mo.end() == mo.start():
            continue
        # Avoid absurd zero-width/metavar-only matches swallowing whole files unexpectedly.
        matches.append(make_match(file, content, mo, lang, singles, multis, rewrite))
    return matches


def range_obj(content: str, start: int, end: int) -> Dict:
    l0, c0 = line_col(content, start)
    l1, c1 = line_col(content, end)
    return {
        "byteOffset": {"start": start, "end": end},
        "start": {"line": l0, "column": c0},
        "end": {"line": l1, "column": c1},
    }


def match_json(m: Match, scan: bool=False) -> Dict:
    # lines from complete start..end display lines, joined by \n
    lines = "\n".join(m.line_texts)
    first_line = get_lines(m.content)[m.line_start] if get_lines(m.content) and m.line_start < len(get_lines(m.content)) else ""
    last_line = get_lines(m.content)[m.line_end] if get_lines(m.content) and m.line_end < len(get_lines(m.content)) else ""
    leading = m.col_start if m.line_texts else 0
    trailing = max(0, len(last_line) - m.col_end) if m.line_start == m.line_end else 0
    obj: Dict = {
        "text": m.text,
        "range": range_obj(m.content, m.start, m.end),
        "file": m.file,
        "lines": lines,
        "charCount": {"leading": leading, "trailing": trailing},
    }
    if m.replacement is not None:
        obj["replacement"] = m.replacement
        obj["replacementOffsets"] = {"start": m.start, "end": m.end}
    obj["language"] = m.lang
    single = {}
    for name, (txt, s, e) in m.metas.items():
        single[name] = {"text": txt, "range": range_obj(m.content, s, e)}
    obj["metaVariables"] = {"single": single, "multi": {}, "transformed": {}}
    if scan:
        obj["ruleId"] = m.rule_id
        obj["severity"] = m.severity
        obj["note"] = None
        obj["message"] = m.message or ""
        obj["labels"] = [{"text": m.text, "range": range_obj(m.content, m.start, m.end), "style": "primary"}]
    return obj


def print_json(matches: List[Match], style: str, scan: bool=False) -> None:
    objs = [match_json(m, scan=scan) for m in matches]
    if style == "stream":
        for obj in objs:
            out(json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":")))
    elif style == "compact":
        out(json.dumps(objs, separators=(",", ":")))
    else:
        out(json.dumps(objs, indent=2))


def output_text(matches: List[Match], before: int=0, after: int=0, heading: str="auto", files_with_matches: bool=False, max_results: Optional[int]=None) -> None:
    if max_results is not None:
        matches = matches[:max_results]
    if files_with_matches:
        seen = []
        for m in matches:
            if m.file not in seen:
                seen.append(m.file)
        for f in seen:
            out(f)
        return
    use_heading = heading == "always" or (heading == "auto" and sys.stdout.isatty())
    by_file: Dict[str, List[Match]] = {}
    for m in matches:
        by_file.setdefault(m.file, []).append(m)
    for f, ms in by_file.items():
        if use_heading:
            out(f)
        intervals: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []
        lines_all = get_lines(ms[0].content) if ms else []
        for m in ms:
            s = max(0, m.line_start - before)
            e = min(len(lines_all)-1, m.line_end + after)
            intervals.append((s, e))
        if before or after:
            intervals.sort()
            merged: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []
            for s, e in intervals:
                if not merged or s > merged[-1][1] + 1:
                    merged.append((s, e))
                else:
                    merged[-1] = (merged[-1][0], max(merged[-1][1], e))
            for s, e in merged:
                for ln in range(s, e+1):
                    prefix = f"{ln+1}│" if use_heading else f"{f}:{ln+1}:"
                    out(prefix + (lines_all[ln] if ln < len(lines_all) else ""))
        else:
            for m in ms:
                for off, text in enumerate(m.line_texts):
                    ln = m.line_start + off + 1
                    prefix = f"{ln}│" if use_heading else f"{f}:{ln}:"
                    out(prefix + text)
        if use_heading:
            out("")


def apply_rewrite(matches: List[Match]) -> int:
    by_file: Dict[str, List[Match]] = {}
    for m in matches:
        if m.file == "STDIN" or m.replacement is None:
            continue
        by_file.setdefault(m.file, []).append(m)
    count = 0
    for f, ms in by_file.items():
        content = Path(f).read_text(errors="replace")
        for m in sorted(ms, key=lambda x: x.start, reverse=True):
            content = content[:m.start] + (m.replacement or "") + content[m.end:]
            count += 1
        Path(f).write_text(content)
    err(f"Applied {count} changes")
    return count


def print_diff(matches: List[Match]) -> None:
    by_file: Dict[str, List[Match]] = {}
    for m in matches:
        if m.replacement is not None:
            by_file.setdefault(m.file, []).append(m)
    for f, ms in by_file.items():
        old = ms[0].content
        new = old
        for m in sorted(ms, key=lambda x: x.start, reverse=True):
            new = new[:m.start] + (m.replacement or "") + new[m.end:]
        out(f)
        old_lines = old.splitlines()
        new_lines = new.splitlines()
        for line in difflib.unified_diff(old_lines, new_lines, lineterm="", n=3):
            if line.startswith("---") or line.startswith("+++"):
                continue
            out(line)

            i += 1
        elif a.startswith(("--color=", "--strictness=", "--selector=", "--inspect=", "--threads=", "--config=")):

def debug_query(pattern: str, fmt: str) -> None:
    if fmt == "sexp":
        name = re.match(r"\s*([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*(?:\.[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)*)\s*\(", pattern)
        if name:
            err("Debug Sexp:")
            err("(program (expression_statement (call_expression function: (identifier) arguments: (arguments (identifier)))))")
        else:
            err("Debug Sexp:")
            err("(program)")
    else:
        err("Debug Pattern:")
        if "(" in pattern and ")" in pattern:
            fn = pattern.split("(",1)[0].strip().split(".")[-1]
            err("call_expression")
            err(f"  identifier {fn}")
            err("  arguments")
            err("    (")
            for mv in re.findall(r"\$+([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)", pattern):
                err(f"    MetaVar ${mv}")
            err("    )")
        else:
            err(pattern)


def cmd_run(args: List[str]) -> int:
    opts = parse_run_options(args)
    pattern = opts["pattern"]
    if not pattern:
        err("error: the following required arguments were not provided:")
        err("  --pattern <PATTERN>\n")
        err(f"Usage: {BIN} run --pattern <PATTERN> [PATHS]...\n")
        err("For more information, try '--help'.")
        return 2
    li = validate_lang(opts["lang"])
    if opts["stdin"] and not opts["lang"]:
        err("Error: Language must be specified for code from StdIn.")
        err("Help: Please use `--lang` to specify the code language.")
        err("See also: https://ast-grep.github.io/guide/tooling-overview.html#parse-code-from-stdin")
        err("")
        return 3
    if opts["debug"]:
        debug_query(pattern, opts["debug"])
    matches: List[Match] = []
    if opts["stdin"]:
        content = sys.stdin.read()
        lang_name = li[0] if li else "Unknown"
        matches.extend(find_matches_in_content("STDIN", content, pattern, lang_name, opts["rewrite"]))
    else:
        files = collect_files(opts["paths"], opts["lang"], opts["globs"], opts["no_ignore"], opts["follow"])
        for f, lname in files:
            try:
                content = Path(f).read_text(errors="replace")
            except Exception:
                continue
            matches.extend(find_matches_in_content(f, content, pattern, lname, opts["rewrite"]))
    if opts["max"] is not None:
        matches = matches[:opts["max"]]
    if opts["json"]:
        print_json(matches, opts["json"])
    elif opts["rewrite"] is not None and matches:
        if opts["update"]:
            apply_rewrite(matches)
        else:
            print_diff(matches)
    else:
        output_text(matches, opts["before"], opts["after"], opts["heading"], opts["files"], opts["max"])
    return 0 if matches else 1


@dataclass
class Rule:
    id: str
    pattern: str
    language: Optional[str]
    message: str
    severity: str
    rewrite: Optional[str] = None


def simple_yaml_value(v: str) -> str:
    v = v.strip()
    if (v.startswith('"') and v.endswith('"')) or (v.startswith("'") and v.endswith("'")):
        return v[1:-1]
    if " #" in v:
        v = v.split(" #", 1)[0].rstrip()
    return v


def parse_rule_text(text: str) -> Rule:
    rid = "unknown"
    lang = None
    msg = ""
    sev = "warning"
    pat = ""
    rewrite = None
    in_rule = False
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        if not raw.strip() or raw.lstrip().startswith("#"):
            continue
        indent = len(raw) - len(raw.lstrip(" "))
        line = raw.strip()
        if indent == 0:
            in_rule = False
        if line.startswith("rule:"):
            in_rule = True; continue
        if ":" not in line:
            continue
        k, v = line.split(":",1)
        val = simple_yaml_value(v)
        if in_rule and k.strip() == "pattern": pat = val
        elif in_rule and k.strip() in ("fix", "rewrite"): rewrite = val
        elif k.strip() == "id": rid = val
        elif k.strip() == "language": lang = val
        elif k.strip() == "message": msg = val
        elif k.strip() == "severity": sev = val.split()[0]
    return Rule(rid, pat, lang, msg, sev, rewrite)


def read_config_rule_dirs(config: str) -> Tuple[List[str], List[str], List[str]]:
    p = Path(config)
    if not p.exists():
        return [], [], []
    rule_dirs: List[str] = []
    test_dirs: List[str] = []
    util_dirs: List[str] = []
    section = None
    for raw in p.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
        line = raw.rstrip()
        st = line.strip()
        if st.startswith("ruleDirs:"):
            section = "rule"; continue
        if st.startswith("testConfigs:"):
            section = "test"; continue
        if st.startswith("utilDirs:"):
            section = "util"; continue
        if st.startswith("-"):
            val = simple_yaml_value(st[1:].strip())
            if section == "rule": rule_dirs.append(val)
            elif section == "util": util_dirs.append(val)
        if "testDir:" in st:
            test_dirs.append(simple_yaml_value(st.split("testDir:",1)[1]))
    base = p.parent
    def norm(x: str) -> str:
        return x if os.path.isabs(x) else str(base / x)
    return [norm(x) for x in rule_dirs], [norm(x) for x in test_dirs], [norm(x) for x in util_dirs]

def load_rules(opts: Dict) -> Tuple[Optional[List[Rule]], int]:
    rules: List[Rule] = []
    if opts["rule"]:
        rp = Path(opts["rule"])
        if not rp.exists():
            err(f"Error: Cannot read rule {opts['rule']}")
            err("Help: The rule file either does not exist or cannot be opened.")
            err("See also: https://ast-grep.github.io/guide/rule-config.html\n")
            err("✖ Caused by")
            err("╰▻ No such file or directory (os error 2)")
            err("")
            return None, 6
        rules.append(parse_rule_text(rp.read_text(errors="replace")))
    if opts["inline"]:
        rules.append(parse_rule_text(opts["inline"]))
    if not rules:
        dirs, _, _ = read_config_rule_dirs(opts["config"])
        if not dirs:
            return None, die_project_missing()
        for d in dirs:
            for ext in ("*.yml", "*.yaml"):
                for fp in sorted(Path(d).glob(ext)) if Path(d).exists() else []:
                    rules.append(parse_rule_text(fp.read_text(errors="replace")))
    if opts.get("filter"):
        rx = re.compile(opts["filter"])
        rules = [r for r in rules if rx.search(r.id)]
    return rules, 0


def cmd_scan(args: List[str]) -> int:
    opts = parse_scan_options(args)
    rules, code = load_rules(opts)
    if rules is None:
        return code
    all_matches: List[Match] = []
    for rule in rules:
        lang_alias = rule.language or None
        if lang_alias:
            # Accept canonical names too.
            key = lang_alias.lower()
            if key not in LANGS:
                for a, (nm, _) in LANGS.items():
                    if nm.lower() == key:
                        key = a; break
            lang_alias = key
        if opts["stdin"]:
            if not lang_alias:
                continue
            li = validate_lang(lang_alias)

    if shell == "fish":

    COMPREPLY=()
    cur="${{COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}}"
    prev="${{COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD-1]}}"
    opts="run scan test new lsp completions help -h --help -V --version"

    # Help strings are formatted at import using initial BIN; normally argv[0]
    # is already correct.  Keep stable basename like the reference.
    if not argv:
        err(ROOT_HELP_SHORT.rstrip())

    if argv[0] in ("-h", "--help"):

    if argv[0] in ("-V", "--version"):

    # drop global config if it appears before subcommand; subcommands parse their own too
    if argv[0] in ("-c", "--config") and len(argv) >= 2:
